 Atla Tadde 2026: Date, Puja Timings, Rituals and Significance
 By IE Author - October 27, 2026 
 Source: ChatGPT 
 Atla Tadde is a special festival celebrated by Telugu women in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Every year, women and young girls come together to pray, apply henna, enjoy traditional swings and prepare Atlu, a type of dosa. This year, Atla Tadde 2026 falls on Wednesday, October 28. The festival is dedicated to Goddess Gauri, also known as Goddess Parvati. Married women pray for their husbands’ health and long life, while unmarried women traditionally seek blessings for a suitable life partner. 
 Here is everything you need to know about the Atla Tadde 2026 date, puja timings, rituals, traditions and significance. 
 What Is Atla Tadde and Why Is It Celebrated? 
 Atla Tadde is a traditional Telugu festival that celebrates faith, family and married life. The word Atlu refers to the dosas prepared during the festival, while Tadde refers to Tritiya, the third lunar day. 
 On this day, married women observe Atla Tadde Vratam and pray to Goddess Gauri for their husbands’ health and a happy family life. Unmarried girls also take part in the festival and traditionally seek blessings for a suitable life partner. 
 But the celebration is not only about fasting and prayers. Women spend time with family members, sing traditional songs and share food. These customs make Atla Tadde an important part of Telugu culture. 
 Atla Tadde 2026 Date and Puja Timings 
 Atla Tadde, also called Atla Taddi, takes place during the Telugu month of Ashwayuja. Families celebrate it on Krishna Paksha Tritiya, the third lunar day after the full moon. 
 Here are the important details:

 Festival name 
 Atla Tadde or Atla Taddi

 Devotees usually perform Gauri Puja in the evening and break their fast after moonrise, according to their family traditions. 
 Atla Tadde 2026 Puja Timings 
 According to the Hyderabad Panchang, the Tritiya Tithi begins at approximately 4:06 AM on October 28 and ends at 1:06 AM on October 29, 2026. In Hyderabad, the moon is expected to rise at around 7:39 PM on October 28. 
 These are tithi and moonrise timings, not a separate auspicious puja muhurat. Women traditionally perform Gauri Puja in the evening and break their fast after moonrise. Timings may vary by city, so check your local Telugu Panchangam for the appropriate puja muhurat. 
 Atla Tadde 2026 Significance 
 Atla Tadde has a special place in many Telugu households. Devotees believe that worshipping Goddess Gauri on this day brings peace, happiness and blessings to the family. The festival is mainly associated with three traditions: 
 Prayers for married life: Married women pray for their husbands’ health and long life. 
 Blessings from Goddess Gauri: Unmarried girls traditionally pray for a caring life partner. 
 Family traditions: Mothers and grandmothers teach younger family members about the festival and its customs. 
 Atla Tadde also gives families a chance to spend time together and celebrate traditions passed down through generations. 
 Atla Tadde Puja Vidhanam: How to Celebrate at Home 
 Families follow different customs while celebrating Atla Tadde. However, these are some common rituals followed in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. 
 Wake up early: Women traditionally wake up before sunrise and eat a simple meal before beginning their fast. In some families, this includes rice with curd and pickle. 
 Apply Gorintaku: Women and girls decorate their hands with Gorintaku, or henna. Many also enjoy traditional swings called Uyyala and sing Telugu folk songs. 
 Prepare Atlu: Families prepare small dosas called Atlu. These are an important part of the festival and are offered to Goddess Gauri. 
 Perform Gauri Puja: In the evening, devotees clean the prayer area, light a diya and offer flowers, turmeric, kumkum, fruits and Atlu to Goddess Gauri. The exact timing and sequence may vary by family tradition. 
 Listen to the Vratam Katha: Families read or listen to the traditional story connected with Atla Tadde. Elders often explain the meaning of the festival to younger family members. 
 Offer prayers to the moon: After moonrise, devotees traditionally offer water and prayers to the moon. They complete the remaining puja and Vayanam rituals according to family customs before breaking their fast. 
 Perform Vayanam: Women offer Atlu and other traditional gifts to married women as Vayanam and seek their blessings. 
 The order of rituals and the number of offerings may differ between families. 
 Atla Tadde Puja Items List 
 If you are planning to perform Atla Tadde Puja at home, you can prepare the commonly used items in advance. 
 Picture or idol of Goddess Gauri, or a turmeric representation of the Goddess according to family custom 
 Turmeric and kumkum 
 Fresh flowers 
 Diya and incense sticks 
 Rice and fruits 
 Atlu (small dosas) 
 Betel leaves and areca nuts 
 Water for moon worship 
 Traditional Vayanam items 
 Some families also prepare special offerings based on their customs. 
 Why Are Atlu and Gorintaku Important During Atla Tadde? 
 Two things that make Atla Tadde special are Atlu and Gorintaku. 
 Atlu (Dosas) 
 Atlu are small dosas made using rice and urad dal batter. Families prepare Atlu as an offering to Goddess Gauri. They also share these dosas with married women during Vayanam. Recipes, preparation methods and the number of Atlu may differ from one family to another. 
 Gorintaku (Henna) 
 Gorintaku, or henna, is a special part of Atla Tadde celebrations. Women and girls apply henna to their hands, often a day before the festival. They also enjoy swings, sing traditional songs and spend time with family and friends. These traditions make the festival more joyful. 
 Atla Tadde Vratam Katha: Traditional Festival Story 
 Atla Tadde has a traditional story that many Telugu families share during the festival. 
 According to one commonly shared version of the story, a young princess observed the Atla Tadde fast but struggled with hunger as the day went on. Her brothers wanted to help her, so they created a light that looked like the moon. Believing that the moon had risen, the princess broke her fast early. 
 Later, when her family searched for a suitable marriage match, she was offered an elderly groom. In the story, she sought help from Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, who explained that her brothers had deceived her with a false moon and that she had broken her fast too early. 
 The princess observed the fast again the following year and waited until the real moon rose. According to the story, she was then blessed with a suitable young husband. 
 Families share this traditional account to teach younger generations about faith, patience and the importance of observing the vratam according to their customs. 
 How Telugu Families Celebrate Atla Tadde Today 
 Atla Tadde is still a special occasion for Telugu families in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Many families start preparing a day before the festival. Women apply henna, get the puja items ready and prepare the ingredients for Atlu. Young girls enjoy swings and sing traditional songs. Elders help with the puja and explain the customs to younger family members. Families also visit relatives and share Vayanam. 
 Telugu families living away from their hometowns celebrate Atla Tadde in their own way. Some follow all the traditional rituals, while others keep things simple with prayers and homemade food. No matter how they celebrate, the festival gives families a chance to come together and remember their traditions. 
 Atla Tadde 2026 falls on October 28. It is a special day for Telugu families to pray, prepare Atlu, apply Gorintaku and spend time together. These traditions help families stay connected to their culture. Whether you celebrate with relatives or at home, Atla Tadde is an occasion to share happiness and blessings with your loved ones.

 Frequently Asked Questions 
 When is Atla Tadde in 2026? 
 Atla Tadde falls on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. It is celebrated on Ashwayuja Krishna Paksha Tritiya. 
 Which Goddess is worshipped during Atla Tadde? 
 Women worship Goddess Gauri, a form of Goddess Parvati. They pray for a happy family life and the well-being of their loved ones. 
 Can unmarried girls observe Atla Tadde Vratam? 
 Yes. Unmarried girls also celebrate Atla Tadde and traditionally pray for a suitable life partner. 
 Why are Atlu important during Atla Tadde? 
 Atlu are small dosas prepared for the festival. Families offer them to Goddess Gauri and share them with married women as part of Vayanam. 
 When do women break the Atla Tadde fast? 
 Women traditionally break their fast after seeing the moon and completing their evening prayers. The time depends on moonrise in their city and their family customs. 
 What are the main rituals of Atla Tadde? 
 The main rituals include fasting, Gauri Puja, preparing and offering Atlu, applying Gorintaku, listening to the Vratam Katha, worshipping the moon and performing Vayanam. 
 What items are needed for Atla Tadde Puja? 
 Common puja items include a picture or idol of Goddess Gauri, turmeric, kumkum, flowers, a diya, incense sticks, fruits, rice, Atlu and water for moon worship. Items may vary by family tradition.
